analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (28 October 2026)
key_insights: US equities rose Tuesday: S&P 500 +0.60% to 7722.60, Nasdaq +1.18%, Dow +0.03%. Breadth was mixed and equal-weight RSP lagged the cap-weighted index by about 60 bp. Semis, memory and neoclouds led.

The AI rally was attributed to removal of funding overhangs and renewed focus on compute/capex demand ahead of this week's hyperscaler earnings. Lower oil on diplomacy hopes also helped, though concern remains about a near-term return to kinetic activity.

Broadcom finalized a $63B debt financing package, the largest AI infrastructure debt deal, to fund TPU procurement for Anthropic over five years. Broadcom had to negotiate higher interest rates and provide financial guarantees to protect lenders against Anthropic default risk.

The Broadcom deal eases some AI financing fears after Monday's Meta $95B equity raise and SpaceX's $40B debt raise. Sentiment remains fragile, and some investors see the coming Anthropic IPO as the next test of AI firms' ability to raise capital.

The October FOMC statement is due Wednesday at 2pm ET, with a 2:30pm Warsh press conference. Analysts expect a hold, then a hike in December and possibly March. Two dissents are seen as likely (Hammack and Logan), with Kashkari a possibility.

Key FOMC statement question is the 'timelier return' of inflation to target sentence. Some analysts expect it to be removed, while Goldman suggests it could be expanded. Warsh is seen giving no explicit guidance, though he might hint at a December move.

Iran diplomacy showed little concrete progress. Headlines about US military preparations and Trump saying he is near a critical decision keep expectations for renewed kinetic action elevated. WTI settled down 1.8%, back below $100/barrel.

October consumer confidence rose to 91.7 from 84.2, well above the 81.0 consensus. Year-ahead inflation expectations fell but remain elevated at 5.8%. Consumers planned less spending on services and durables.

Preliminary September durable goods orders rose 1.8% m/m vs 1.5% consensus, the largest increase since Apr-26. Core capital goods shipments rose 1.2% vs 0.8% consensus, while core capital goods orders rose 0.5% vs 0.7% consensus.

September new home sales were 676K vs 650K consensus. FHFA house prices rose 0.3% m/m in August vs 0.2% consensus. ADP weekly private payrolls averaged +16.75K jobs/week over four weeks, decelerating for a second straight week.

Earnings themes: AI infrastructure, data center demand, pricing power, input costs, a resilient but bifurcated consumer, and limited spillover from higher rates. CLS, CDNS, UPS, RCL, SPGI, NUE and HRI raised guidance or beat. BA, XYL, AWI, HUBB (utility segment) and WSO disappointed.

Reports said the FTC could sue to block Cintas's proposed $5.5B acquisition of UniFirst (UNF -10.5%). GM will move its listing to Nasdaq effective 17-Nov, which gives eligibility for Nasdaq-100 inclusion.
Treasuries were flat to slightly weaker at the short end (yields up 1-2 bp) and the 5Y auction tailed. The dollar index rose 0.3%, gold rose 0.9% and Bitcoin futures rose 1.0%.

European equities rose: Germany +0.7%, France +0.5%, UK -0.8% (FTSE lagged on weak earnings). Basic resources, technology and construction led. Autos and oil & gas lagged. Bund yield 3.37%, gilt 5.35%.

Bank of America is negative on the Stoxx 600 and projects about 10% further downside by Q2 2027. It is underweight semis, capital goods and mining and overweight defensive 'anti-AI' food/beverage and household goods. Citi flagged rising bearish bets, with shorts added in the Dax and Euro Stoxx 50.

Constructive European views: Rothschild expects Stoxx 600 EPS growth of about 19.1% this year and 8.9% in 2027 at about 13.9x earnings. UBS forecasts about 15% earnings growth in 2026 and 2027, and BCA recommends buying Europe. Goldman said equal-weighted earnings are 1.8% above expectations with about 30% of MSCI Europe reported.

ECB Q3 bank lending survey showed higher rates reducing loan demand across all segments, with housing loan demand at a net -27% vs -15% in Q2. The ECB is expected to hold on Thursday, with focus on whether it will lean against rising French bond yields.

French consumer confidence fell to 80 in October (consensus 85), the lowest since July 2013. French 10-year yields hit their highest since 2002 last week. JPMorgan sees about 5% of GDP in fiscal adjustment needed and the OAT-Bund spread about 55 bp too wide versus fundamentals. It prefers non-French exposure and non-French banks. Bank of America upgraded French equities to overweight in mid-October on valuation.

UK BRC shop price inflation rose to 2.1% y/y, a two-year high, vs 1.6% consensus. The UK Budget is Wednesday, with a living wage rise of about 3.9%, removal of import taxes on 100 products and an extension of the fuel duty freeze. Fiscal space is forecast to fall to about £15B from about £24B. Talks with the EU on closer alignment add speculation about an early election.

Asia: Nikkei +1.73%, Hong Kong -0.73%, China -1.33%. South Korea Q3 GDP rose 1.0% q/q vs 0.8% consensus. The Bank of Korea said chip exports could fall $50-100B from earlier forecasts if US tech capex slows in 2027, and Taiwan's central bank warned 2027 growth will moderate.

China industrial profits rose 14.4% y/y in September (August 4.2%), helped by 5% y/y PPI growth, the fastest since 2022. Gains were concentrated in electronics and mining while consumer sectors stayed weak.
TSMC is reportedly planning to raise CoWoS packaging prices by up to 20%. The EU is planning safeguard measures (caps or tariffs) on more Chinese imports, possibly from Q1-27.

BOJ Watcher survey: 16 of 33 see a 1.75% terminal rate, 10 see 2.00%, and 45% now see 2% or higher. Meiji Yasuda plans to buy about JPY2T of JGBs in FY26, concentrated in superlongs, double its initial plan. The RBNZ is expected to hike 25 bp to 3.00% on 28-Oct.

market_movers.rationale: DA Davidson upgraded from neutral to buy. At 16x earnings the market discounts a scenario where neither the Anthropic nor OpenAI deal materializes and earnings have peaked. The $63B financing confirmed Broadcom was awarded the Anthropic ASIC.
Big Q3 beat led by Compute & Storage. FY27 revenue guide is about 11% above consensus, and customer demand forecasts for 2028 are meaningfully higher than for 2027.
Q3 beat and FY26 guidance raised by more than the beat. Record $8.23B backlog, +18% y/y recurring revenue, and a new $2.5B buyback authorization.
Q3 EPS missed and Commercial Airplanes margins were weaker, though FCF beat. 777X first delivery timeline maintained for 2027.
Q3 revenue missed, organic growth flat vs about 3%+ guided, and FY guidance lowered.

sector_views.rationale: Bank of America projects about 10% further downside by Q2 2027. It is underweight semis, capital goods and mining and overweight food/beverage and household goods. Rothschild, UBS and BCA are more constructive.
Bank of America upgraded to overweight on valuation in mid-October. JPMorgan prefers non-French domestic exposure and non-French banks.

CDNS Q3 (reported 10/27): results ahead of consensus, FY26 guidance raised by more than the beat, backlog $8.23B.
UPS Q3 (reported 10/27): EPS beat, FY revenue and EPS guidance raised.
BA Q3 (reported 10/27): EPS missed, FCF better than expected, Commercial Airplanes margins weaker.
XYL Q3 (reported 10/27): revenue missed, EPS largely in line, FY guidance lowered.
HRI Q3 (reported 10/27): big earnings beat, revenue in line, FY26 guidance midpoints raised.
SOFI Q3 (reported 10/27): EBITDA, EPS and revenue beat, FY26 forecasts raised.
JBLU Q3 (reported 10/27): EPS and revenue missed, FY26 ASM and operating margin guidance cut, RASM forecast raised.
HLT Q3 (reported 10/27): RevPAR and EPS beat but revenue light, EBITDA in line, Q4 guide light.
WSO Q3 (reported 10/27): sales in line, gross margin missed by about 80 bp, EPS nearly 9% below.
HUBB Q3 (reported 10/27): EPS and revenue beat on Electrical Solutions/data center, FY26 outlook raised, Utility Solutions missed.
NOVN Q3 core EPS $2.46 reported vs $2.29 consensus, FY26 core operating income outlook raised.
P911 9M EPS €2.06 reported vs €0.13 year-ago, FY26 forecast confirmed.
ORA Q3 EBITDAaL €4.14B reported vs €4.10B consensus, FY growth guidance raised to above +4.5%.
BEI Q3 revenue €2.36B reported vs €2.38B consensus, organic growth -1.3%.
HSBA Q3 revenue missed on slower wealth growth, $1B buyback announced, outlook unchanged.
MBG cut FY26 guidance to adjusted return on sales of 2-3% from 3-5%.
Goldman: about 30% of MSCI Europe reported, equal-weighted earnings 1.8% above expectations, EPS estimates up 2.1% over the past month. Morgan Stanley: +13% weighted beat skew vs +31% last quarter.

Citi flagged rising bearish bets in Europe, with shorts added in the Dax and Euro Stoxx 50 and the prior week's inflows reversing.
Bank of America noted the sharpest cyclical-to-defensive rotation in Europe since the Covid shock.

The EU is planning safeguard measures (import caps or tariffs) on Chinese goods, possibly from Q1-27, after a hybrid vehicle cap deal.
French protests and fiscal worries, with student leaders vowing to continue despite Macron's concessions.
Britain is holding talks with the EU on closer alignment and possible return of free movement, with a 20-Nov summit.
Prolonged Middle East conflict is cited as a risk for oil, inflation and Japanese JGB demand.
